WBCD: University of Wisconsin investigators; computer-aided diagnosis of fine-needle aspirate cytology [29].
Coimbra: University of Coimbra investigators; prediction of breast cancer from routine blood biomarkers [10].
SEER (5-year and survival): National Cancer Institute SEER program (population cancer surveillance) [32]; public research extraction by Namdari [31].

WBCD: 30 nuclear morphology features (mean, standard error and worst value of 10 measurements).
Coimbra: 9 clinical and metabolic variables (age, BMI, glucose, insulin, HOMA-IR, leptin, adiponectin, resistin, MCP-1).
SEER (5-year and survival): 12 clinical and demographic variables (16 features after one-hot encoding); survival time and vital status used only to define outcomes.

Coimbra: 2009–2013; University Hospital Centre of Coimbra, Portugal.

WBCD: Digitised cytology images; operator-initialised boundary tracing, so measurements are partly operator-dependent.
Coimbra: Fasting blood samples and routine clinical measurements.
SEER (5-year and survival): Registrar abstraction; vital status by linkage with vital statistics; cause of death not recorded.

WBCD: Sampling scheme not documented in detail.
Coimbra: Case–control: newly diagnosed, untreated cases and healthy controls.
SEER (5-year and survival): Women with infiltrating ductal or lobular carcinoma, aged 30–69 years, node-positive; exclusions for unknown tumour size, unexamined nodes and survival under 1 month. For the 5-year label, 754 patients alive with under 60 months of follow-up were excluded.

WBCD: Historical, single-centre, operator-dependent measurements; near-separable classes.
Coimbra: Very small sample (EPV 5.8) and case–control design, so probabilities do not transfer to screening.
SEER (5-year and survival): No treatment, HER2 or comorbidity data; all-cause mortality only; restricted age and nodal status; coarse race categories (Other combines American Indian/Alaska Native and Asian/Pacific Islander); possible bias from excluding censored patients.
Methodological benchmarking of registry-based prognostic modelling; not for estimating population survival.
